0|0eb79294dbe328debae67961df28113141825d7b|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"btrfs: dio iomap DSYNC workaround
iomap dio will run generic_write_sync() for us if the iocb is DSYNC.
This is problematic for us because of 2 reasons:
1. we hold the inode_lock() during this operation
generic_write_sync()
2. we hold a read lock on the dio_sem but take the write lock in fsync
Since we don't want to rip out this code right now
locking is a bit much to do at this point
this masterpiece of a patch.
First
column2: we clear DSYNC on the iocb so that the iomap stuff doesn't know

column1: that it needs to handle the sync.  We save this fact in
current->journal_info
column2: because we need to see do special things once

column1: we're in iomap_begin
column2: and we have no way to pass private information

column1: into iomap_dio_rw().
Next we specify a separate iomap_dio_ops for sync
->end_io() callback that gets called when the dio completes.  This is
important for AIO
column2: because we really do need to run generic_write_sync()

column1: if we complete asynchronously.  However if we're still in the submitting
context when we enter ->end_io() we clear the flag so that the submitter
knows they're the ones that needs to run generic_write_sync().
This is meant to be temporary.  We need to work out how to eliminate the
inode_lock() and the dio_sem in our fsync and use another mechanism to
protect these operations.
